data.narrative:
Causaly, a Series B biotech and health company founded by Yiannis Kiachopoulos and Artur Saudabayev, has raised $95M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 3 public companies (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers, with direct stage-comparable benchmarks including Colossal Biosciences ($10.3B), Chai Discovery ($3.8B), and New Limit ($3.1B).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression applies a 1.9x multiplier to the $95M total raised proxy, yielding $180M. Peer-median valuation across the 3 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields $3.8B, with the peer range spanning $3.1B to $10.3B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (8.1x median across the biotech sector) cannot be applied absent disclosed revenue figures. The resulting triangulated range is $153M (low), $2.0B (median), to $4.4B (high).

The wide dispersion reflects stage uncertainty: stage-progression suggests a conservative near-term bridge valuation, while peer-median reflects the upper band of recently capitalized Series C peers. Key uncertainties include Causaly's revenue trajectory, capital efficiency relative to peers, and whether recent Series C benchmarks (2024) remain anchored or face compression. A $1.5B–$3.0B range appears supported by the peer median and upper-stage progression scenarios, pending validation of product adoption and runway.
